experiments.title: Identify and remove the retained fine-only solver critical path before another multilevel variant
experiments.evidence: N24 and N25 local multilevel both lose full ticks despite reduced iteration counts; N25 removes most redundant shuffle work but still costs81.2ms impact and630.8ms debris versus36.6ms and380.6–387.5ms controls. Existing census shows anchored components own>99% node updates, and intact warm components already skip iterations. Aggregate maximum iterations do not identify the end-of-kernel active tail.
experiments.proposed_mechanism: Measure per-component start/end and iterative work in a separate diagnostic retained-control build; determine whether a few difficult anchored components serialize the end of the tick. If confirmed, redistribute their existing fine solve within the same tick using GPU-owned scheduling, retaining original equations and convergence. Compare against current work stealing before inventing a new queue.
experiments.estimate_qualification: Unestimated until active-tail wall-time exposure is measured; maximum iterations and source stalls are not a time budget. No implementation experiment should begin before this prerequisite.
experiments.confidence: Evidence supports investigating smaller/sparse late-stage imbalance, but weakens this as the main large-city target. Do not prioritize a large-city scheduling rewrite without stronger evidence.
experiments.experiment_cost: Bounded diagnostic record per component and source audit; preserve exact physical comparisons and measure timings in separate uninstrumented builds.
experiments.supporting_measurements: A material stress-kernel tail with low concurrent useful components, reproduced across large active scenarios; original quality holds after redistribution and full-step time falls.
experiments.refuting_measurements: Balanced component finish times, high useful work throughout, or scheduling/coordination costs exceed the tail. Choose factor reuse or lifecycle batching instead.
experiments.architecture_benefit: Decouple logical component ownership from GPU scheduling while preserving same-tick convergence; only pursue if measured concurrency evidence supports it.
experiments.existing_record_audit: Offline reuse of current census shows max/mean recorded CTA cycles at initial impact trial/correction: city25 1.09/2.54, city64 1.14/1.31, city256 1.16/1.15. experiments.title: Remove sequential emulation of multi-CTA coarse row work inside local components
experiments.evidence: Rejected N24 bridge spends1137.56ms of1153.47ms profiled tick in componentStressSolve. Large same-row cooperative layout was copied into local component execution. See n24-equation-profile.json.
experiments.proposed_mechanism: Use concurrent local row workers and remove empty multi-CTA tile reductions; retain every bond contribution, FP64 arithmetic, settled skipping, convergence and current-tick correction. Preserve cooperative global path as a distinct ownership case. Independent dense-cycle/symmetry/linearity checks must verify any changed addition tree; do not silently weaken accepted physical bounds.
experiments.confidence: High evidence of redundant local scheduling; low-to-medium probability of beating retained implementation after hierarchy costs. Savings are hypotheses, not profiler subtraction.
experiments.experiment_cost: Isolated local ownership CUDA change and matched mathematical checker extension if addition order changes; targeted long-row/self-column cases, full cycle/math/sanitizers, rebuilt native checks, light A/B/A; full52/warm only for finalists.
experiments.supporting_measurements: Substantially fewer shuffle/reduction instructions and shorter local kernel with unchanged operator accuracy and physical work, plus lower complete ticks than retained control.
experiments.refuting_measurements: Correctness/quality regressions, long-row performance losses, construction cost or remaining cycle cost still outweighs fewer iterations; no net full-step benefit.
experiments.architectural_benefit: Separates per-component row ownership from cooperative grid ownership; makes future Tile row operations express useful work rather than emulate unused global tiles.
experiments.conclusion: Removing sequential coarse-row tile emulation substantially reduces the rejected N24 overhead, but remains much slower than retained fine-only control on bridge, chain, impact, large idle and debris. Dense control is neutral; stimulus has no consistent improvement. Original impact/debris force/health failures remain. No candidate promotion or warm/full52 extension.
